name: LA-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+20 partisan lean makes this deeply Republican turf
Scalise's incumbency, seniority, and roughly 19-to-1 fundraising edge ($11.0M vs $0.58M)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 96 percent
No general-election polls or expert ratings exist, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The district's R+20 baseline, Scalise's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Republican win; with no polls or expert ratings available, fundamentals carry the forecast and the Democrat has no visible path to closing a twenty-point gap.
model.watch: A major national wave toward Democrats or an unforeseen development involving the incumbent could narrow the margin, but nothing in the current evidence points that direction.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 1st District, anchored in the New Orleans suburbs, leans Republican by roughly twenty points. Steve Scalise, a top House Republican leader, is seeking another term with a commanding financial edge: he has raised about $11 million and holds nearly $3 million on hand, while Democrat Lauren Jewett has raised about $580,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a four percent chance.

The fundamentals point firmly to Scalise. The district's partisan baseline, his incumbency advantage, and his fundraising dominance all favor the Republican side, and the independent and second Republican candidates are unlikely to change the outcome even under Louisiana's primary system. The race sits firmly in Safe Republican territory, with the main uncertainty stemming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive contest.
